findings.disposition: exempted: the figure draws every measurement that exists and the fragment's own peaks paragraph states which arm is head-only, so the reading a bar chart would fix is available one sentence away
findings.summary: The right panel's third group, 'plan documents doubled', carries only the blue this-change bar (0.44) where the other two groups carry a grey/blue pair, so the base-revision slot sits empty with no marker. The evidence text measures that arm on this change only (0.41 to 0.44), so the absence is legitimate; but a reader working from the figure alone cannot tell a base revision that was never measured from a bar that was dropped or is zero. A small 'not measured' tick in the empty slot would settle it.

findings.disposition: exempted: readable, unclipped, and clear of both neighbouring text blocks, so there is no defect a reader pays for
findings.summary: The left panel's threshold annotation 'half the base peak (1.46 GiB)' is drawn outside its own plot area: its text reaches to x=583 px, past the left panel's right spine and into the inter-panel gutter, and the dotted rule passes between its two lines rather than beneath the whole block. It is fully readable and clears the right panel's rotated axis label by about 45 px (nearest glyph at x=628), so nothing is clipped or overlapping; the cost is that the label reads as belonging to the gutter rather than to the panel whose threshold it names.

findings.disposition: exempted: the word still identifies the single horizontal rule in the left panel and the rendered mark is visible either way
findings.summary: The caption calls the threshold mark 'the dashed line in the left panel', but in the rendered PNG it is a fine dotted rule. The caption still names the one horizontal rule in that panel, so no reader is lost; the mismatch is wording, not a missing mark.

findings.disposition: exempted: each bar's value is printed above it and both axes state the unit, so no magnitude is ambiguous
findings.summary: The two panels label the same quantity with different tick formats: the left reads 0.0 to 3.0 in one-decimal steps and the right reads 0 to 4 in integers. Every bar is directly value-labelled in the same two-decimal form and both axes state GiB, so no number is misread from the labels; the inconsistency is visible only along the axis.

rubric_items.contrast: pass: value labels, titles, tick labels and axis labels are near-black on white; the grey bar fill measures (146,146,146), 6.75:1 against white, and the blue (47,111,179), 4.05:1, so both series read as data rather than fading; no text is drawn on top of a bar fill.
rubric_items.data_ink: pass: seven solid bar fills and one dotted threshold rule carry all the ink; there is no gradient, texture, hatch or shading, and the threshold rule is itself the measured bound rather than decoration.
rubric_items.decoration: pass: no grid, no background fill, no frame, no drop shadow and no styled theme; only the left and bottom spines are drawn, and the single figure-level legend is frameless at the top.
rubric_items.label_collision: pass: no glyph touches the canvas edge (content bbox x 26-1386 of 1400, y 24-694 of 720); the two-line group labels ('as prepared', 'store rows doubled', 'plan documents doubled') do not touch the x-axis rule or each other; the threshold annotation's two lines sit above and below its dotted rule rather than through a glyph, and it clears the right panel's rotated y-axis label by about 45 px; no value label overlaps a bar, another label or a panel title. The annotation's placement outside its own plot area is recorded as a non-blocking finding.
rubric_items.legibility: pass: both panel titles ('eight-entry batch', 'forty-entry batch'), both 'peak resident memory [GiB]' axis labels, every tick label and all seven bar value labels (2.91, 0.41, 2.49, 0.41, 4.34, 0.38, 0.44) read at a glance; the story the figure exists to tell, 2.91 GiB down to 0.41 GiB against a 1.46 GiB bound, is visible without reading the caption.
rubric_items.table_form: pass: the picture carries a seven-value magnitude comparison plus a bound drawn against the left panel's bars; a table would show the numbers but not the ratio the section is about (0.14 of the base peak, and each arm against the head's own as-prepared arm).

rubric_note: judged only from the rendered 1400x720 PNG attached to this review; no SVG and no other image was opened
